title: Annotation intake: write human annotation to SqliteLibrary (Rust binary, M1 near-term path)
description:
Implements DESIGN.md §9.4 near-term annotation capture for M1.

Per sub-decisions (#13): M1 uses a Rust binary subcommand. Python CLI wrapper deferred to M2+.

Binary subcommand (extends alcanzai binary from #18):
  alcanzai annotate --library <path.db> --object <KnowledgeObjectId> "<annotation text>"

Behavior:
  - Look up the target KnowledgeObject by ID (returns error if not found).
  - Create a new KnowledgeObject with content_type: 'annotation', title: 'Annotation on <target title>', blocks: [one paragraph block with the annotation text], relationship to target stored in the relationships table (predicate: 'annotates', subject: annotation_id, object: target_id).
  - Ingest via Library::ingest (NewUnique path — annotations have no stable external ID; content_hash of the text is the anchor).

Integration test:
  - Seed a KnowledgeObject, annotate it, rebuild vault → annotation note appears in vault with correct wikilink back to the source object.
  - Delete vault, rebuild → annotation note still appears (it was never vault-native).

This is the §9.4 done-condition: human-authored content survives delete-and-regenerate because it lives in the Library.

Acceptance criterion: alcanzai annotate command works; annotation note projected into vault; delete+rebuild test passes.
